exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier for a countable noun.
exercises.prompt: There are ___ students absent today — only two.
exercises.explanation: 'A few' = a small positive number → used with countable nouns. 'A little' = uncountable. 'Much' = uncountable. 'Less' = uncountable or formal comparative.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier for an uncountable noun.
exercises.prompt: She has ___ experience in project management.
exercises.explanation: 'Little' = small amount (uncountable) — 'experience' is uncountable. 'A few/many/fewer' are for countable nouns.

options: There is a little water left in the bottle.
Few students submitted their assignments on time.
She has less experience than her colleague.
There are less participants than expected.
exercises.answer: There are less participants than expected.
exercises.explanation: 'Participants' is countable — use 'fewer', not 'less'. 'Less' is for uncountable nouns. 'Fewer participants' is correct.

options: All of the above are correct.
exercises.answer: All of the above are correct.
exercises.explanation: 'Both the students', 'Both of the students', and 'Both students' are all correct. 'Both' works with or without 'the' or 'of the'. All three forms are acceptable.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier meaning 'the entire group'.
exercises.prompt: ___ the members agreed to the new policy.
exercises.explanation: 'All of the members' = every single one (more than two). 'Each of' = considered individually. 'Both of' = exactly two. 'Neither of' = negative (for two).

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct determiner for indicating which one.
exercises.prompt: I'll take ___ book — the one on the right.
exercises.explanation: 'That book' = singular + distant (pointing to one further away or specified 'the one on the right'). 'This' = near. 'These/Those' = plural.

exercises.instruction: Identify the error in the sentence.
exercises.prompt: Every students must submit their assignment by Friday.
options: Should be 'Every student' — 'every' takes a singular noun.
Should be 'All students' — 'every' is wrong here.
exercises.answer: Should be 'Every student' — 'every' takes a singular noun.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' is always followed by a singular noun and singular verb: 'Every student must submit.' 'Every students' (plural) is incorrect.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier for a large amount (uncountable).
exercises.prompt: There is ___ traffic in the city during rush hour.
exercises.explanation: 'A lot of' works with both countable and uncountable nouns. 'Traffic' is uncountable → 'a lot of traffic'. 'Many' requires countable nouns.

exercises.instruction: Translate: 'Tidak ada mahasiswa yang datang terlambat.' → English:
exercises.explanation: 'No + noun' as a determiner: 'No students came late.' 'None' is a pronoun (no noun follows): 'None of them came late.' 'Neither' = exactly two options.

exercises.instruction: Choose 'each' or 'every' — referring to members of a group individually.
exercises.prompt: ___ student received a personalised feedback report.
exercises.explanation: 'Each student' (focus on individuals separately) and 'Every student' (all considered as a group) are both grammatically correct here. 'All' requires plural: 'All students received'.

exercises.prompt: Neither of the students have submitted their work.
options: Should be 'has submitted' — 'neither of' takes singular verb.
Should be 'None of' — 'neither' is for two only.
exercises.answer: Should be 'has submitted' — 'neither of' takes singular verb.
exercises.explanation: 'Neither of' is grammatically singular → singular verb: 'Neither of the students has submitted their work.' (Note: 'their' as singular pronoun is acceptable.)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier for a negative context (uncountable).
exercises.prompt: There wasn't ___ time left for questions.
exercises.explanation: 'Much' = large amount (uncountable) — used in negatives and questions. 'Time' is uncountable. 'Many/few/a few' are for countable nouns.

exercises.prompt: I have never seen ___ dedication in a student before.
exercises.explanation: 'Such + uncountable noun' (without article): 'such dedication'. 'Such a' is for singular countable nouns: 'such a dedicated student'. 'Dedication' is uncountable.

exercises.prompt: ___ three proposals were rejected by the committee.
exercises.explanation: 'Both' = exactly two. 'All' = three or more. Since there are three proposals → 'All three proposals.' 'Neither' = negative for two.
'Sebagian besar' = most (the majority). 'Most students' = more than half. 'All' = 100%; 'Each' = individually; 'Both' = two only.
